item.stem:

- Point P is at coordinates (3, 2).
- Point Q is at coordinates (3, -2).
- Point R is at coordinates (-3, -2).
- Point S is at coordinates (-3, 2).

reference_items.stem:
[Image: Coordinate grid with points M and N]

Two points M and N are shown in the figure above. John is looking for a point P such that MNP is an isosceles triangle. Which of these points could be point P?
reference_items.figure_description: A 6-by-6 grid in the first quadrant of a Cartesian coordinate system. The horizontal x-axis has an arrow pointing to the right, labeled x, with origin O and tick marks labeled 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. The vertical y-axis has an arrow pointing upwards, labeled y, with tick marks labeled 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. Grid lines are drawn at each integer value from 1 to 6. Two points are plotted on the grid: point M at (1, 2), labeled M, and point N at (5, 2), labeled N.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Which angle in the figure has a measure closest to 45°?

[Image: Circle divided into angles p, q, r, and s]
reference_items.figure_description: A circle contains a vertical diameter dividing it into left and right halves. From the center, two additional line segments (radii) are drawn: one extending to the left edge at roughly 9 o'clock (slightly below horizontal), and another extending down and to the right at approximately a 45-degree angle from the vertical. Four central angles are labeled: angle q is in the upper-left quadrant (between the upward vertical radius and the left radius, roughly 90°); angle p is in the lower-left quadrant (between the left radius and the downward vertical radius, roughly 90°); angle r is in the upper-right (between the upward vertical radius and the lower-right radius, an obtuse angle of roughly 135°); and angle s is in the lower-right (between the downward vertical radius and the lower-right radius, roughly 45°).
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Rectangle PQRS can be rotated (turned) onto rectangle UVST.

[Image: Rectangles UVST and PQRS]

What point is the center of rotation?
reference_items.figure_description: Two adjacent congruent rectangles forming an L-like shape. Rectangle UVST is oriented vertically, with vertices U (bottom left), V (bottom right), S (top right), and T (top left). Rectangle PQRS is oriented horizontally, extending to the right from the upper portion of rectangle UVST: vertex S is at the top left (shared with UVST), R is at the top right, Q is at the bottom right, and P is at the bottom left, lying on the vertical line segment SV between S and V. Each vertex is marked with a black dot.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.stem:
[Image: A numbered axis, from 0 to 2. Two dots are shown, “P” and “Q”. “P” lies roughly halfway between 0 and 1 and “Q” lies roughly three fourths between 0 and 1.]

P and Q represent two fractions on the number line above.

P × Q = N.

Which of these shows the location of N on the number line?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: A numbered axis from 0 to 2 where “P” lies roughly halfway between 0 and 1, “Q” lays roughly three fourths between 0 and 1, and “N” lies halfway between 1 and 2.]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: A numbered axis from 0 to 2 where “P” lies roughly halfway between 0 and 1, “Q” lies roughly three fourths between 0 and 1, and “N” lies after Q but before 1.]

options.label: C

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: A numbered axis from 0 to 2 where “P” lies roughly halfway between 0 and 1, “Q” lies roughly three fourths between 0 and 1, and “N” lies in between 0 and P.]

reference_items.figure_description:
The figure above the text shows a horizontal number line with an arrow at the right end. There are tick marks labeled 0, 1, and 2, with equal spacing between 0 and 1 and between 1 and 2. Between 0 and 1, two points are marked with black dots: point P is labeled below the line at approximately 0.5 (halfway between 0 and 1), and point Q is labeled below the line at approximately 0.75 (three-fourths of the distance from 0 to 1).

Each of the four response options shows the same number line with points P and Q in their original positions, along with a third point labeled N above the line:
- Option A: Point N is marked halfway between 1 and 2, at approximately 1.5.
- Option B: Point N is marked between Q and 1, at approximately 0.85.
- Option C: Point N is marked between P and Q, at approximately 0.625.
- Option D: Point N is marked between 0 and P, at approximately 0.25.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.figure_description:
Stem: A Cartesian coordinate system with dashed axes and arrows at each end; the origin is marked with a point labeled O. A shaded right-like scalene triangle is located in the first quadrant with its vertical base lying on the positive y-axis and its third vertex pointing to the right.
Option A: The coordinate plane with the triangle's base along the positive x-axis and the third vertex pointing downward into the fourth quadrant.
Option B: The coordinate plane with the triangle's base along the negative y-axis and the third vertex pointing to the right into the fourth quadrant.
Option C: The coordinate plane with the triangle's base along the negative x-axis and the third vertex pointing upward into the second quadrant.
Option D: The coordinate plane with the triangle's base along the negative y-axis and the third vertex pointing to the left into the third quadrant.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
